parsed.answer: Source [11899391] directly supports the claim: an autoimmune disease-associated IL2RA haplotype (linked to type 1 diabetes) correlates with diminished IL-2 responsiveness in CD4+ T cells (reduced STAT5a phosphorylation), lower FOXP3 expression in Tregs, and reduced suppressive function, while Tregs from type 1 diabetes and other autoimmune patients are deficient in controlling autologous proinflammatory responses. Source [13923140] corroborates the broader link between impaired IL-2/IL-2 pathway and reduced CD4+CD25+ Treg function causing autoimmunity, though it concerns reduced IL-2 production rather than Treg responsiveness specifically.
